<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A compact subset ${\mathcal K}\subset {\mathbb R}^n$, $n\ge 2$, is called a {\em Kakeya set} if it contains a unit-line segment pointing
in every direction.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thmBe}
There are Kakeya sets  ${\mathcal K}\subset {\mathbb R}^n$ of {\em measure zero}, $|{\mathcal K}|=0$.  
Additionally, there are planar 
revolvable
sets of {\em arbitrarily small area}.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
Let $n\ge 2$.  Then if ${\mathcal K}$ is a Kakeya set in ${\mathbb R}^n$,
\begin{equation}\label{2.14}
\dim {\mathcal K}=n,
\end{equation}
with $\dim$ denoting either Minkowski dimension, $\dim_M$, or, more importantly,
Hausdorff dimension, $\dim_H$.
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
If ${\mathcal K}\subset {\mathbb R}^2$ is a Kakeya set then
$\dim {\mathcal K}=2$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm3.1}
If ${\mathcal K}$ is a Kakeya subset of ${\mathbb R}^3$, then it must have full dimension, both Minkowski and
Hausdorff.  Thus, $\dim_M{\mathcal K}=\dim_H{\mathcal K}=3$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm3.2}
Given $\varepsilon>0$ there is a constant $c_\varepsilon>0$ so that whenever ${\mathbb T}_\delta=\{T\}$ is a collection of
$\delta$-separated $\delta$-tubes with $\delta\in (0,1/2)$, we have
\begin{equation}\label{3.1}
\bigl| \, \bigcup_{T\in {\mathbb T}_\delta} T\, \bigr| \ge c_\varepsilon \delta^\varepsilon \, \bigl( \, |{\mathbb T}_\delta|\cdot |T|\, \bigr).
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm3.3}  Sticky Kakeya subsets of ${\Bbb R}^3$ have full dimension.
  Additionally, \eqref{3.1} is valid if the $\delta$-direction separated collection ${\mathbb T}_\delta$ is sticky.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{KT}
A collection of $\delta$-tubes ${\mathbb T}_\delta$ satisfies the {\bf Katz-Tao} condition if
\begin{equation}\label{3.6}
\sup_{{\mathcal C}\subset {\Bbb R}^3, \, \, \text{convex}} \Delta({\mathbb T}_\delta, {\mathcal C})\lesssim 1.
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{F}
A collection of $\delta$-tubes ${\mathbb T}_\delta$ satisfies the {\bf Frostman} condition if
\begin{equation}\label{3.7}
\sup_{{\mathcal C}\subset {\Bbb R}^3, \, \, \text{convex}} \Delta({\mathbb T}_\delta, {\mathcal C})\lesssim 
\Delta({\mathbb T}_\delta,B).
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
(Strong Kakeya: Katz-Tao version)\label{thmkt}
If ${\mathbb T}_\delta$ as above is {\em Katz-Tao}, then \eqref{3.1} is valid,   i.e.,
                                           
                  
\begin{equation}\label{3.8}
\bigl| \, \bigcup_{T\in {\mathbb T}_\delta} T\, \bigr| \ge c_\varepsilon \delta^\varepsilon \, \bigl( \, |{\mathbb T}_\delta|\cdot |T|\, \bigr), \quad \forall \, \varepsilon>0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
(Strong Kakeya: Frostman version)\label{thmf}
If ${\mathbb T}_\delta$ as above is {\em Frostman}, then 
                                                      
\begin{equation}\label{3.9}
\bigl| \, \bigcup_{T\in {\mathbb T}_\delta} T\, \bigr| \ge c_\varepsilon \delta^\varepsilon, \quad \forall \, \varepsilon>0.
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thmgwz}   If $n=2$, then
\begin{equation}\label{4.7}
\|F\|_{L^4({\mathbb R}^2\times {\mathbb R})} \lesssim_\varepsilon   \delta^{-\varepsilon} 
\bigl\| \, \bigl(\sum_{J\in \text{Part}_{\delta^{1/2}} [-1,1]} |P_JF|^2 \, \bigr)^{1/2} \, \bigr\|_{L^4({\mathbb R}^2\times {\mathbb R})}
 \, , \, \forall \, \varepsilon>0, \, \, \,
\text{if } \, \, \text{supp } \Hat F\subset \Gamma_\delta.
\end{equation}
Consequently, both \eqref{4.3} and \eqref{4.4} are valid when $n=2$.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
